document.tekst_begin: Nationale biogrondstoffenstrategie 2026 Boodschap Biogrondstoffen zijn cruciaal om invulling te geven aan menselijke behoeften. Vanzelfsprekend als bron van voedsel, maar ook voor gebruik in materialen en als energiebron. In de toekomst neemt het belang van biogrondstoffen verder toe, omdat ze een belangrijke rol vervullen als duurzame vervanger van fossiele grondstoffen in een weerbare, klimaatneutrale en circulaire economie. Dit vraagt om een andere manier van omgaan met biogrondstoffen: een ander gebruik en een verandering in aanbod en verwerking van biogrondstoffen. Het betekent gedragsverandering, een ander consumptiepatroon, ander landgebruik en andere industrie. Er ontstaan nieuwe routes, nieuwe verdienmodellen en nieuwe toepassingen voor het gebruik van biogrondstoffen. We werken toe naar een duurzaam systeem, gericht op brede welvaart en met respect voor ecologische grenzen. Zo ontstaat een systeem dat burgers voorziet van een breed scala aan waardevolle producten en nieuwe perspectieven biedt aan ondernemers in de landbouw, de industrie, de bouw en andere sectoren. document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2026–2027 Aanhangsel van de Handelingen Vragen gesteld door de leden der Kamer, met de daarop door de regering gegeven antwoorden 56 Vragen van het lid Van der Lee (PRO) aan de Minister van Buitenlandse Zaken over de staatsbegrafenis voor oorlogsmisdadiger Ratko Mladic´ in Servië (ingezonden 31 augustus 2026). Antwoord van Minister Berendsen (Buitenlandse Zaken) (ontvangen 21 september 2026). document.tekst_begin: Non-Paper by Estonia, Finland, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden and Czechia on the Cyber Security Act 2 Guiding principles to make the ICT supply chain mechanism work We welcome the Commission’s proposal to mitigate cybersecurity risks at EU level. The Cybersecurity Act 2, more speciﬁcally the introduction of a new European framework for securing ICT supply chains, directly aƯects cybersecurity, strategic dependencies and the functioning of the internal market. Having a risk-based approach underpinned by thorough risk analyses is a strong foundation to enhance the EU’s resilience. We would therefore like to underline our support for the objectives of this framework, as it is in our view the most pragmatic and coherent way to face the threats and manage those risks that aƯect the Union. We also support moving first with a phase out on mobile networks, building on the experience with the 5G Cyber Security Toolbox. However, further risk assessments are needed when it comes to the fixed and satellite networks. document.tekst_begin: Paper by the Netherlands – A Multilateral Instrument for European resilience and Value-chain Autonomy Proposal for a comprehensive approach to coordinating targeted finance to reinforce the EU's open strategic autonomy Introduction • The Netherlands believes rapid developments on the world stage compel the EU to reduce high-risk strategic dependencies to strengthen European resilience and its open strategic autonomy. Where those developments confront us with attestable resilience and autonomy externalities, we should work together to enable our industries to counter those externalities by developing necessary capabilities they do not (sufficiently) provide. That means creating market activity insufficiently present or altogether absent, inasmuch warranted to protect ourselves from undue foreign influence infringing on the EU’s autonomy. In the view of the Netherlands, that means certain well-targeted State aid should be approved in earnest under the conditions presently set out, within the purview of a new, dedicated Multilateral Instrument for European Resilience and Value-chain Autonomy (MINERVA). document.tekst_begin: 1 Nationaal Plan Energiesysteem 2026: wetenschappelijke reflectie 20 oktober | dr. ir. Het beschrijft de ontwikkeling van het gehele Nederlandse energiesysteem op het pad van de energietransitie en biedt daarbij vele nuttige inzichten. Dat onderstaande reflectie een aantal kritische noten bevat, doet niet af aan de waardering voor het uitgevoerde werk en moet vooral gezien worden als een oproep het volgende NPE, in 2029, nog beter te maken. Met het geactualiseerde Nationaal Plan Energiesysteem (hierna: NPE 2026) wil het kabinet richting en duidelijkheid geven wat betreft de uitvoering van de energietransitie en de daartoe noodzakelijke beleidsmaatregelen. document.tekst_begin: Aanleiding Op 10 september 2026 heeft de commissie voor Volkshuisvesting en Ruimtelijke Ordening van de Tweede Kamer verzocht te reageren op een brief van Kavel 10 B.V. Kavel 10 is een Nederlands geo-bedrijf. In deze brief uit Kavel 10 zorgen over het lopende traject van de Basisvoorziening Beeldmateriaal (BVBM), met name over de onzorgvuldige voorbereiding, dreigende marktverstoring en het ontbreken van een onafhankelijke toets. Kavel 10 geeft aan direct geraakt te worden door de ontwikkelingen van BVBM. De voorgenomen uitwerking dreigt volgens Kavel 10 een functionerende Nederlandse marktsector te verdringen. Het verzoek is het traject te pauzeren tot een onafhankelijke toets van nut, noodzaak, juridische grondslag en marktimpact heeft plaatsgevonden, en tot de meest geraakte marktpartijen formeel zijn gehoord. De BVBM is primair gericht op het structureel borgen van reeds bestaande luchtfoto’s en hoogtebestanden (AHN) van Nederland. Een eventuele verbreding waar de brief zich op richt zit nog in de verkennende fase, er is nog geen concreet voorstel uitgewerkt. Op 23 oktober jl. is gesproken met Kavel 10. Hierbij waren aanwezig. document.tekst_begin: Aan Staatssecretaris TER BESLISSING Datum 26 oktober 2026 Onze referentie IENW/BSK-2026/195868 Opgesteld door DG Mobiliteit Dir.Openbaar Vervoer en Spoor Rijksinfrastructuur Beslistermijn 27-10-2026 Bijlage(n) 4 Pagina 1 van 2 Kamerbrief Landelijke uitrol ERTMS Aanleiding In april van dit jaar is het rapport verkennende analyse landelijke uitrol samen met de 24e voortgangsrapportage ERTMS1 aan de Kamer aangeboden. De conclusies uit het rapport en het gesprek wat u op 27 mei jl. heeft gehad met de Kamer2 hebben aanleiding gegeven om de landelijke uitrol van ERTMS uit te werken. Vanuit de sector is hierop een notitie opgesteld die ondersteunend is aan het vaststellen van de koers in de landelijke uitrol. Daarnaast informeert u, overeenkomstig met de Regeling Grote Projecten, de Kamer elk halfjaar over de ontwikkelingen binnen het programma ERTMS (European Rail Traffic Management System). Geadviseerd besluit Instemmen met het verzenden van de kamerbrief over de landelijke uitrol van ERTMS, in combinatie met de 25e voortgangsrapportage en uw appreciatie daarop als bijlagen. Het rapporteurschap moet de vaste Kamer commissie voor Infrastructuur en Waterstaat (hierna: commissie IenW) helpen de Nederlandse inzet in de Europese onderhandelingen te controleren en te sturen. Het pakket moet grensoverschrijdende en multimodale reizen eenvoudiger maken. De voorstellen betreffen onder meer de toegang tot reis - en ticketinformatie, de verhouding tussen vervoerders en platforms, technische interoperabiliteit en de bescherming van reizigers bij verstoringen. Hartland Box A8188 Oder 20 2491 DC DEN HAAG Datum 5 november 2026 Betreft Uw brief van 12 augustus 2026 inzake centrale registratie van stalongelukken Pagina 1 van 2 Directoraat-generaal Agro Directie Dierlijke Agroketens en Dierenwelzijn Bezoekadres Bezuidenhoutseweg 73 2594 AC Den Haag Postadres Postbus 20401 2500 EK Den Haag Overheidsidentificatienr 00000001858272854000 T 070 379 8911 (algemeen) F 070 378 6100 (algemeen) www.rijksoverheid.nl/lvvn Ons kenmerk DGA-DAD / 108551060 Geachte mevrouw Hartland, Ik heb uw brief van 12 augustus jl. over het ontbreken van een centrale registratie van stalongelukken in goede orde ontvangen. Mijn excuses voor het feit dat dit antwoord langer op zich heeft laten wachten dan gebruikelijk. Met deze brief reageer ik op de door u genoemde zorgen. Met de Kamerbrief worden twee toezeggingen afgedaan. Deze toezeggingen vragen in de kern om de Tweede Kamer te informeren over de resultaten het monitoringstraject (TZ202606-123, TZ202403-071). Gemeenten en provincies: zij zijn eigenaar en opdrachtgever van de omgevingsdiensten. Omgevingsdiensten zijn daarom afhankelijk van het bevoegd gezag om robuust te worden. items.titel: Research on Emission Inventory and Emission Reduction Benefits Assessment of Non-Road Construction Machinery in Tangshan Port
items.samenvatting_bron: This study investigated the emission inventory and reduction strategies of non-road construction machinery in Tangshan Port. A Portable Emission Measurement System (PEMS) was used to collect operating condition data and measure pollutant emissions from 16 pieces of machinery under real-world operating conditions. Based on the field measurements, emission factors for typical construction machinery in Tangshan Port were established. The emission reduction effects and cost-effectiveness of different scenarios of phase-out and Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) emission control ratios for China III emission standard non-road construction machinery at Tangshan Port were analyzed. The results showed that the estimated annual operating hours of excavators, loaders, forklifts, and bulldozers in the port were 3.51, 4.87, 3.44, and 2.34 times the corresponding values recommended in the “Technical Guidelines for the Compilation of Emission Inventories of Non-road Mobile Pollution Sources (Trial)”, respectively, indicating relatively high utilization intensity. Emissions of PM, NOx, HC, and CO from port construction machinery were mainly attributable to excavators and loaders, with combined contribution rates of 66.65%, 68.58%, 60.89%, and 59.85%, respectively. items.titel: Clubmosses (Lycopodiaceae, Lycopodiales) in the Herbarium Collection of the Croatian Natural History Museum (CNHM): implications for nature conservation
items.samenvatting_bron: During the curation of the Herbarium Collection of the Croatian Natural History Museum – CNHM, special attention was given to clubmosses (Lycopodiaceae), which are of conservation concern – they are all listed in Annex V of the EU Habitats Directive and in Croatia their commercial collection is regulated, except for two species that are strictly protected. Results show that the collection contains 115 herbarium sheets of clubmosses with 221 herbarium specimens, which include 99 inventory numbers. Lycopodium clavatum is the most numerous in terms of inventory numbers and herbarium sheets and Huperzia selago in terms of herbarium specimens. Clubmosses were collected over a period of 127 years, with the greatest intensity of their collection in the first decades of the 20 th century and in the period of the 1960s and 1970s. The largest number of clubmosses was, expectedly, collected in Croatia. Clubmosses were collected by 16 collectors and identified by nine identifiers. Material of clubmosses stored in the CNHM Herbarium Collection is predominantly old and does not cover their entire known distribution area in Croatia. However, the curated data can be used for preparing the report on the conservation status of species according to the Habitats Directive, as well as for extinction risk assessment. They are an important source of evidence for the presence of plant species in a given area at a specific point in time.

items.titel: Pollinator-promoting wildflower fields attract farmland birds and rodents, depending on spatial configuration and landscape context
items.samenvatting_bron: To mitigate the decline of pollinators in farmlands, a widely used approach is to establish wildflower fields. Their effects beyond pollinators, however, require further investigation in Central-Eastern Europe, even regarding popular taxa such as birds, and potential pest species such as rodents. We established wildflower plantings in two spatial configurations (one field or three strips with the same area per plot) in both homogeneous and heterogeneous agricultural landscapes in Central Hungary. We found that fields increase bird species number, individual number and Shannon-diversity in homogeneous agricultural landscapes, but not in heterogeneous landscapes, which in general are more diverse regardless of wildflower plantings. Also, wildflower fields promote rodents compared to arable fields. Thus, wildflower fields may have a wide range of biodiversity benefits beyond pollinators depending on field area and landscape context. These results provide evidence from Central-Eastern Europe to support the implementation of the European Union's Nature Restoration Regulation.

items.titel: Successfully Implementing ESG Practices at India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL): A Case Analysis
items.samenvatting_bron: Case analysis provides insights into the successful integration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles at India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL), a premier government-owned financial institution (FI) dedicated to supporting the development of sustainable infrastructure in India. IIFCL has emerged as a leader in sustainable finance by embedding ESG considerations into its investment decision-making, risk assessment, and governance frameworks. The case highlights key strategic initiatives, including the adoption of ESG risk screening tools, alignment with international sustainability standards, and the promotion of green infrastructure projects. Through stakeholder engagement, internal capacity-building, and policy innovation, IIFCL has demonstrated how innovative financial solutions can effectively balance developmental mandates with long-term environmental and social sustainability. The study provides insights into the challenges, enablers, and measurable outcomes of IIFCL’s ESG journey, acting as a paradigm for other institutions aiming to incorporate ESG frameworks into infrastructure financing.

items.titel: From Riverbank to Region: Green–Blue Infrastructure, Cultural Heritage and Ecotourism Spatial Integration in Bihor County, Romania
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change, urban heat islands and climate hazard risks are putting pressure on tourism in the historic quarters. This study assesses the spatial preconditions for a resilient ecotourism infrastructure in Bihor County, Romania. By examining ecological and cultural resources and low-impact accessibility across three scales (the county, the metropolitan area and the city of Oradea, particularly its historic quarter), together with land surface temperature variations, the study identifies the weakest points in the region’s ecotourism potential. A multi-scale GIS framework was applied, overlaying ecosystem services, blue–green infrastructure (BGI) components, cultural heritage assets and land surface temperature (LST) data. The results indicate that Bihor County holds a fragmented but genuine foundation for an ecotourism network, with the Crișul Repede River as the main connector. GBI can support low-impact ecotourism routes within Oradea, but only partially in the current configuration, as the historic quarter presents insufficient green connectivity. Moreover, the most important ecological areas are vehicle dependent. The multi-scale assessment further reveals a complex interdependency between tourism potential, urban planning policy, mobility infrastructure and climate exposure.

items.titel: Phenology-Aware Urban Vegetation Mapping with Multi-Temporal PlanetScope Imagery and Machine Learning
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban vegetation plays a crucial role in regulating microclimates, mitigating the urban heat island effect, improving air quality, and contributing to climate resilience—functions increasingly vital amid accelerating climate change. Despite this importance, mapping vegetation in urban environments remains challenging, particularly at the species level, due to structural complexity, mixed land use, and spectral similarity among vegetation types. In this study, we developed a hierarchical multi-temporal framework using high-resolution (3 m) PlanetScope imagery with time-series analysis to classify urban vegetation and dominant tree species by capturing their phenological trajectories. PlanetScope imagery from 2021 to 2023 was first averaged into monthly composites. These monthly composites were subsequently organized into annual multi-temporal feature stacks (Y.C.), seasonal multi-temporal feature stacks (S.C.), individual seasonal datasets, and monthly datasets. Spectral bands were combined with five vegetation indices (NDVI, EVI, GNDVI, MSAVI, and NIRv) to represent seasonal variations in vegetation characteristics. A Random Forest classifier was applied at the pixel level. The Y.C. yielded the highest performance for broad vegetation classification (Overall Accuracy = 94.33%, Kappa = 0.92), followed by S.C., while individual seasons and months generally produced lower accuracies. items.samenvatting_bron: Urban trees are important components of green infrastructure, contributing to biodiversity conservation, climate regulation, and carbon storage. Quantifying the composition, structure, and carbon storage capacity of urban tree communities is therefore important for sustainable urban planning and climate change mitigation. This study evaluated species composition, diversity, structural characteristics, biomass, carbon storage, and the economic value of stored carbon in 15 Temmuz National Garden, Kahramanmaraş, Türkiye. A complete inventory of the tree community was conducted, and dendrometric variables, including tree height, crown width, diameter at breast height (DBH), stem dimensions, and bark thickness, were measured. Branch, leaf, and bark samples were collected, and biomass and carbon storage were estimated using the KARBİYOSİS (Carbon Storage and Biomass Calculation System) software. items.titel: The Role of Blue - Green Infrastructure in Restoring the Quality of Urban Spaces in Degraded Areas
items.samenvatting_bron: Contemporary cities are increasingly faced with the need to regenerate derelict and post - industrial areas, while also dealing with the effects of climate change, environmental degradation and rising expectations regarding the quality of life in urban spaces. Processes such as deindustrialisation, suburbanisation and spatial fragmentation have contributed to the emergence of vast urban landscapes characterised by a loss of function, environmental pollution, a lack of public spaces and a weakening of local social identity. In response to these challenges, blue - green infrastructure has become one of the key elements of contemporary spatial planning and sustainable urban regeneration. The aim of this article is to analyse the role of blue - green infrastructure in the process of restoring and improving the quality of urban space in degraded areas. items.titel: Reconsidering The 15 - Minute City in Post - Socialist Urban Contexts : The Case of Rzeszow, Poland
items.samenvatting_bron: Contemporary urban policies increasingly promote the concept of the 15 - minute city as a model for sustainable, resilient, and human - centered urban development. Nevertheless, the practical implementation of this concept in dynamically developing medium - sized cities in Central and Eastern Europe remains insufficiently explored. In many post - socialist urban environments, transformation processes continue to prioritize transport efficiency, investment pressures, and spatial expansion, frequently marginalizing issues related to accessibility, social inclusiveness, environmental quality, and the everyday usability of public spaces. This paper critically examines the applicability of the 15 - minute city concept using Rzeszow — one of the fastest - growing regional cities in south - eastern Poland — as a case study. The study integrates previous research conducted by the authors concerning inclusive urban design , accessibility of public and historic spaces, pocket parks, green and blue infrastructure, and environmentally responsive architectural solutions. Particular attention is given to the relationships between pedestrian accessibility, public - space quality, multifunctional urban furniture, environmental resilience, and the needs of vulnerable social groups, including older adults and people with disabilities. items.titel: Monitoring deep-sea fish biodiversity via a direct deep-water intake from 612 m: Insights into taxonomic composition and temporal dynamics revealed by eDNA metabarcoding
items.samenvatting_bron: We investigated the taxonomic composition and temporal dynamics of deep-sea fish assemblages off subtropical Kume Island, Japan, using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding of water samples from a fixed deep-water intake system. Over 26 months (December 2020–February 2023), 60 high-volume samples (20 L each) were collected from an intake mouth located near the seafloor of the continental slope at 612 m depth during six sampling events. MiFish metabarcoding identified 283 deep-sea fish taxa. Comparison with a regional checklist showed high overlap at family and genus levels but limited species-level overlap. The eDNA dataset included bathydemersal taxa alongside pelagic and mesopelagic groups (e.g., Myctophidae, Stomiidae), which were proportionally more prominent than in the regional checklist. Despite relatively stable environmental conditions at 612 m, NMDS and PERMANOVA revealed significant differences in community composition among sampling events. The February 2023 assemblage showed the greatest separation from the other events. The similarity between December 2020 and December 2021 suggests that seasonal processes may contribute to the observed temporal variation, but the present sampling design does not establish a recurring annual cycle. These findings highlight the potential of intake-based eDNA monitoring as a repeatable framework for detecting broad-scale ecological shifts in the deep ocean.

items.titel: High-density environmental DNA metabarcoding reveals fine-scale three-dimensional structure of a fish community in a semi-closed bay
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal fish assemblages are influenced by environmental heterogeneity across horizontal and vertical dimensions, yet their fine-scale three-dimensional structure remains poorly understood. We investigated spatial variation in fish assemblages using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding at 100 stations across three depth layers (300 samples) in Maizuru Bay, a semi-enclosed coastal bay in Japan. Concurrent hydrographic measurements were used to examine associations between fish assemblage composition and environmental conditions. We detected 216 fish species, with mean species richness decreasing from 28.4 at the surface to 16.4 at the bottom. Thirty-three species were detected exclusively below the surface. Fish assemblage composition differed significantly among depth layers and exhibited pronounced horizontal turnover along the bay axis. Although depth, geographic position, and measured environmental variables were associated with assemblage composition, they collectively explained only 13.0% of the variation. The independent contribution of spatial position (2.9%) exceeded those of depth (0.8%) and measured environmental variables (0.9%). These findings demonstrate substantial three-dimensional heterogeneity in coastal fish assemblages that cannot be fully explained by conventional hydrographic measurements. Our study highlights the importance of integrating horizontal and vertical sampling to characterize coastal fish biodiversity and improve marine ecosystem monitoring.

items.titel: Assessing Urban Development Capacity Under Water Constraints: A Planning - Oriented Index for Spatial Policy
items.samenvatting_bron: Rapid urbanization and increasing pressure on water resources challenge the sustainability of conventional spatial planning practices. Traditional approaches, primarily based on functional zoning and post hoc infrastructure design, often neglect the dynamic relationship between urban development and water availability. This has led to overdevelopment in many regions — particularly coastal and tourism - intensive areas — where water demand exceeds supply capacity, resulting in resource stress and reduced system resilience. This study proposes a novel planning - oriented framework — the Urban Water Adequacy for Development Index (UWADI) — which integrates water resource constraints into the early stages of spatial planning. items.titel: Urban densification to support climate adaptation: balancing costs and agglomeration benefits in the Netherlands
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Where should we build new housing under growing climate hazards? This study develops a framework that balances the economic benefits of density against the geographically varying costs of climate adaptation. We apply it to the Netherlands, where demand for new housing is high, but much of the land lies in floodplains or subsidence-prone areas. Agglomeration benefits are proxied by land values, while adaptation costs are derived from engineering estimates of flood protection and soil subsidence. Combining these data allows us to map spatial trade-offs and identify where development remains welfare-enhancing. Our findings show that dense cities continue to generate strong net welfare gains, even in places with high costs, while low-density settlements generate a welfare loss for new housing. We identify density thresholds above which housing development becomes feasible. Many medium-sized Dutch cities already exceed these thresholds, making densification more beneficial than peripheral expansion. Climate adaptation thus strengthens—rather than weakens—the case for urban densification.

items.titel: Toward bio-inclusive urban design: a relational approach to co-existence
items.samenvatting_bron: Ecological frameworks – such as Nature-based Solutions and Biophilic design – have advanced ecological thinking in urban planning and encouraged nature-connectedness, yet both focus on the utilitarian functions of nature. This externalisation and instrumentalisation of nature as a service provider sparingly acknowledges non-human agency in urban design. Through a targeted purposive scoping review, the paper maps conceptual gaps in these frameworks and explores more-than-human alternatives that support a bio-inclusive approach to urban design. Drawing on ecological empathy and animist awareness, and Freya Mathews’s concepts of conativity and least resistance, the paper argues that a relational understanding is required for an ontological shift to support multispecies co-existence. By conceptually linking ontological foundations with Freya Mathews’s concepts as operating principles, we propose five guiding principles that foreground ethical care, humans as actors, interdisciplinary interdependence, designing for entanglement and detachment, and including epistemological diversity. Together, these would help operationalise a bio-inclusive design framework that supports ecological reciprocity and symbiotic co-existence. The paper contributes to emerging discourse in post-anthropocentric urban planning, multispecies justice, and environmental ethics. It emphasises relationality through a conceptual foundation that can inform design education, policy, and practice.

We conceptualise and operationalise a synthesis between the types of urban NBS trade-offs, processes of compact urbanism and environmental justice dimensions. Using the restoration of the Catharijnesingel canal in Utrecht, the Netherlands, as a case study, we examine the existing trade-offs and how compact urbanism influences them as they arise, evolve, and manifest. This conceptual and analytical framework was applied to the case study using a qualitative approach through interviews, document analysis, and site observations. The research uncovered linkages between governance approaches, the city’s metabolic flows, and socio-spatial antagonisms with the captured urban NBS trade-offs. items.titel: Climate-Resilient Spatial Zoning for Temporary Cultural Infrastructures: A framework for Flood-Prone Contexts
items.samenvatting_bron: Event spaces and cultural areas are often built temporarily. These temporary structures are built without considering the possibility of defending against extreme weather events like floods. Under unforeseen situations like extreme weather, the accessibility and services will collapse. The impact on this will be particularly significant on the vulnerable population, mainly older adults and children. This study will develop a reproducible framework for creating these temporary cultural and event zones that withstand extreme weather events, using the open - source QGIS software. Buffer zones were delineated at distances of 15, 50, and 150 meters from the centre of the river line. The site is divided into three functional zones, based on accessibility, terrain conditions, and risk exposure within the buffer zone. Each zone is then strategically supported with multiple smaller systems spread across the site, nature - based solutions and certain other functions that can operate without disruption during extreme events. These facilities are designed to be close, accessible, and safe for all users, including older adults, people with physical disabilities, and children. The approach offers a low - cost, replicable strategy for climate resilience that can be integrated into temporary cultural and event spaces. This idea can be relevant to projects like Cirk Arena, especially for creating functional, flexible and safe event spaces that can run during extreme weather conditions.

Dat ze kunnen loslaten werd gisteren duidelijk bij inspecties. Specialisten kijken nu of alleen de glasplaten moeten worden verwijderd, of dat de lampen helemaal weg moeten. De weg verbindt Leeuwarden, Heerenveen en Meppel. Verkeer tussen Heerenveen en Leeuwarden wordt omgeleid via Drachten, over de A7 en de N31.
